case_name: Rattan Bai & Anr. v Ram Dass & Ors.
facts: This appeal arises out of the final order dated 8th March, 2011 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Civil Revision No. 1075 of 2011 u/art. 227 of the Constitution of India.
Respondent Nos. 1 to 3 herein instituted a Civil Suit No. RBT 124/22.05.2006 on the file of Civil Judge, Senior Division (S.D.) Jhajjar, against the two appellants herein and two others.
The defendants (appellants herein) contested the suit. They filed a written statement on 2.12.2006.
On 18.12.2007, an application (Annexure P-2) came to be filed purportedly on behalf of the three plaintiffs (respondents 1 to 3 herein), but signed only by respondents 1 and 3 alone.
The trial court did not pass any order either accepting or rejecting the application.
On 4.8.2010, a joint statement (Annexure P-4) of first respondent and the above-mentioned advocate Shri Arun Kumar allegedly representing respondents 1 and 3 herein was recorded by the Trial Court.
In substance, praying that the suit be dismissed in so far as it pertains to respondents Nos. 1 and 3 herein.
issues: Whether the inherent power of the Court was exercised in accordance with the well established principles of law.
Whether the trial court has the power to permit the withdrawal of the applications filed earlier to the withdrawal of the suit.
petitioner_arguments: The mere existence of a power does not justify the exercise of the power.

The issue is not whether the trial court has the power to permit the withdrawal of the applications filed earlier to the withdrawal of the suit but whether such powers was exercised in accordance with law and for the purpose for which it is meant.
respondent_arguments: Nothing prevents the plaintiffs to go back upon the withdrawal.
Even in cases where an application for withdrawal of the suit is allowed, it is held by this Court that nothing prevents the plaintiffs to go back upon the withdrawal.
court_reasoning: The learned trial Court was well within its jurisdiction to allow the withdrawal of application dated 18.12.2007 and statement dated 4.8.2010 under its inherent powers.

In my considered opinion, the impugned order is innocuous and no prejudice will be caused to the defendants-petitioners as they will have full opportunity to present their case before the learned trial Court at the relevant stage.
holding: The High Court dismissed the Revision filed by the appellants herein.
The High Court held - The learned trial Court was well within its jurisdiction to allow the withdrawal of application dated 18.12.2007 and statement dated 4.8.2010 under its inherent powers.
